A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from Generalised Parallel Tempering (GePT) to Accelerated Parallel Tempering (APT). Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original GMM sampling experiments, round-trip rates, normalising-constant estimates and Wasserstein-2 results in Section 4 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 reports original GMM, DoubleWell-4 and ManyWell-32 experiments, including sampling and free-energy results, plus an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck discretisation experiment in Appendix B.2.

M1.justification: V2 adds CMCD-APT with learned transport, interpolation schedules and diffusion coefficients, and introduces bidirectional work-based free-energy estimators. The selected flow-training loss changes from KL plus rejection-rate terms to symmetric KL. Multistep swaps themselves were already present in v1 Appendix D; their reformulation and the GePT/APT renaming are not new components.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates GMM targets only. V2 retains GMM coverage and adds the interacting-particle DoubleWell-4 target, the 65,536-mode ManyWell-32 target, and a one-dimensional Ornstein–Uhlenbeck discretisation test. These substantially broaden the represented distributions and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: V1's comparisons use Linear-PT and Diff-PT baselines. V2 retains these and brings NF-APT and the new CMCD-APT into the joint GMM-10 comparison. Figure 4 additionally evaluates standalone CMCD and Diffusion samplers constructed by concatenating APT's learned transports, substantially expanding the comparison beyond PT baselines.

E3.justification: For GMM diffusion experiments, stated local exploration changes from five HMC updates with two leapfrog steps to one update with five, retaining step size 0.03. Compute normalisation changes from m+2 to K+1 potential evaluations for accelerated swaps. Training pipelines, budgets and chain-count grids are revised, while new experiments introduce free-energy subsampling and neural-sampler testing protocols.

E4.justification: V2 adds a DW-4 case study comparing concatenated neural transports with APT, ManyWell-32 mode-coverage visualisations across chain and acceleration settings, and an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck discretisation-convergence check. V1's GMM normalising-constant and Wasserstein-2 diagnostics are removed. These change the questions investigated and the supporting diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V1's boxplots use five consecutive blocks of 2,000 samples. V2's free-energy boxplots use 30 estimates from random 1,000-sample subsets of 100,000 samples; these are not 30 independent training runs. V2 also adds confidence-interval bars to the Appendix B.2 convergence plot, without specifying their level or construction.

E6.justification: V1's learned GMM-2/10/50 result tables are replaced by a GMM-10 comparison and new DW-4/ManyWell-32 results. For example, v2 Table 1 reports 17 round trips for PT, 194 for NF-APT and 1,743 for CMCD-APT with K=5 at six chains. New free-energy and mode-weight findings appear, while the old GMM log-normaliser and Wasserstein results disappear. Changed protocols preclude treating these as matched performance gains.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's invariance proofs, v2 adds rejection-rate identities, ergodicity and estimator-consistency arguments, acceleration-time convergence bounds, a global communication-barrier limit, and parallelism-versus-acceleration analysis with extensive assumptions and proofs. The revision also introduces internal sign inconsistencies: Equation (4)'s SKL expression conflicts with Equation (3), and Algorithm 1's acceptance work difference reverses Section 3.2's formula.

C1.justification: The retained claim is that neural transports improve PT communication while preserving asymptotic consistency. V2 broadens the principal contributions to include controlled diffusions, theoretical performance scaling and efficient free-energy estimation. Normalising-constant estimation existed experimentally in v1's appendix, but becomes an explicit methodological and theoretical contribution in v2's abstract and main text.

C2.justification: V2 adds barrier-based explanations of when acceleration pays off, a memory-versus-parallelism tradeoff, and explicit limitations involving poor neural training and network-evaluation costs. Its new blanket interpretation of reduced free-energy bias and variance is stronger than Figure 3 supports: the five-chain ManyWell-32 Diff-APT K=1 distribution is visibly more dispersed than PT.

D1.justification: V2 substantially revises and expands implementation documentation, specifying MLP/EGNN architectures, staged data collection and training, method-specific evaluation settings and potential/network-call accounting. Appendices D.7–D.8 newly disclose upstream codebases, licence information and 3090/A100 hardware. These are substantive reproducibility additions, without establishing release of the authors' own implementation.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning through PT/SMC parallelism-time duality and connections to free-energy perturbation, Jarzynski estimators, Bennett acceptance ratios and FEAT. It adds corresponding literature and theoretical references. The acknowledgement of Ballard–Jarzynski's framework and the distinction from Invernizzi's flow-assisted replica exchange remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and mathematical narrative are extensively rewritten around APT, potentials and work. V2 separates the framework, performance analysis and method variants into dedicated sections and reorganises the appendices thematically. The title, terminology and author list also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned to combine a mechanism diagram, sample visualisations and round-trip trajectories. Tables are restructured around round trips, compute-normalised counts, neural calls and barrier estimates. New free-energy, sampler-comparison, convergence and ManyWell visualisations replace or supplement earlier displays; Figure 2 is reformatted with surrounding text, and the old GMM boxplots are removed.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's narrow GMM-only validation with broader experiments, new theoretical analysis and substantially better implementation documentation. However, Algorithm 1 reverses the acceptance work difference stated in Section 3.2, and Equation (4)'s SKL signs conflict with Equation (3). These inconsistencies affect central sampling and training prescriptions, and the PDFs do not establish their relationship to the reported experiments. Together with overstated free-energy interpretations and removed GMM diagnostics, they prevent a reliable judgment that the substantial additions yield a net quality improvement.
